releaseEvidence: Official in-bound commit a0c0acb8 adds group termination across protocol, persistence, settings, conversation UI, backup, and tests.
Official in-bound commits c81f40eb and 2b9126d7 add termination checks and update the terminated-group presentation.
The official v8.5.0 release body discusses member labels and does not announce group termination.
Official follow-up commits 43f19d14, 9702728c, 17faf563, and 562185f4 address termination behavior but are not ancestors of v8.5.0.

implementationEvidence.testEvidenceNote: Tests prove admin eligibility, protocol application, local state updates, known and unknown terminator handling, idempotent refresh, rejection of post-termination peer changes, and backup fixtures containing termination state.

baseFailureEvidence: Neither v8.4.0 nor the newer eligible base v8.4.1 contains the termination protocol fields, termination exception, database column migration, administrator dialog, terminated conversation UI, or focused tests.
The v8.5.0 tree contains the initial end-to-end protocol, persistence, UI, backup, and error-handling implementation.
The later v8.4.2 tag also lacks the feature but is not an ancestor of v8.5.0, so it cannot serve as this task's base.

boundaryAudit.verification: Local read-only git object queries and the official GitHub compare endpoint prove ancestry for the requested boundary; local containment checks prove the effective base and each in-bound feature commit.

reviewReason: The requested 'complete lifecycle' is broader than behavior contained by v8.5.0. Keep this candidate needs_review unless the final boundary is advanced to a tag containing the four post-final commits or the task is explicitly accepted as the initial lifecycle only.
longHorizonSignals: The in-bound task crosses protocol mutation, conflict resolution, local persistence, backup round trips, conversation state, settings eligibility, join errors, and retry UI.
The state graph includes eligibility, two confirmation transitions, in-progress success or failure, retry or cancel, remote convergence, and idempotent terminal handling.
Post-final evidence shows why the word 'complete' cannot be asserted at v8.5.0 without review.
